result.summary: In 2016 Zuckerberg made one dated AI prediction and repeated it: AI will beat humans at perception (vision, hearing, language) within five to ten years. I found it at the China Development Forum (March, news report only), the F8 keynote's 10-year roadmap (April, third-party transcript) and the December Jarvis note (repost), alongside the already-recorded April earnings call. I found no dated or undated statement on when AGI or superintelligence arrives, and the February Döpfner interview could not be read.

reply_text:
I found three 2016 statements, all repeating one claim you already have on file: that within five to ten years AI will be better than people at perception (seeing, hearing, language). I found nothing new on AGI or superintelligence timing, so the "undated" list is empty.

- **19 March 2016, China Development Forum, Beijing:** I only have this from a China Daily report, not his own words. The wording may be the paper's rendering or translation.
- **12 April 2016, F8 keynote:** The quotes come from a third-party transcript on singjupost.com, not Facebook's own page. The official video is on developers.facebook.com, but I didn't open it. The AI line itself doesn't name a date. The "next decade" timing comes from how he framed the whole talk as a 10-year roadmap.
- **About 19 December 2016, "Building Jarvis" note:** He restates that he has "previously predicted" this "within 5-10 years" and says the year made him more confident. I read the note as reposted on techtrends.africa, not on his own Facebook page.

Other things I checked or couldn't reach:
- **27 January 2016 earnings call (Facebook's official transcript):** only says AI breakthroughs are "going to take a long time", with no date, so it doesn't qualify.
- **Late February 2016 interview with Axel Springer chief Mathias Döpfner:** not checked. The repost I opened had only a link, and the Business Insider page was blocked. This is the main gap.
- **July and November 2016 earnings calls, and his late-January 2016 Facebook post on AI:** found but not opened. The 27 April call, behind the existing file, also wasn't opened again.

I used 10 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
